messages:
mira: Heads-up — found a perf regression when switching live traffic to FA v3 for tiny completions (1-8 tokens). Tail latency up ~20-30% p99 under high concurrency (100-400 concurrent requests). I ran a short repro harness and uploaded profiles.
ethan: Can you paste the flame graph / top hotspots? Which kernel path is hot? Any memcpy or kernel-launch churn?
mira: Flame shows FA_v3 fast path dominating, but with a lot of short-lived kernel invocations and memcpy overheads. KV cache eviction spikes correlate with bursts — eviction count ~3x baseline when concurrency >128. Also seeing avg batch size drop to ~1.4 for shortseq traffic.
li: That sounds like batching heuristics went too aggressive on latency. Did we change the batch window or the continuous-batching merge logic in the v3 rollout? Small batches + higher kernel setup cost will kill short seq.
mira: We did experiment: default batch window reduced from 2.0ms -> 0.8ms in the micro-optimizations branch to favor lower latency for longer sequences. Side-effect: tiny sequences no longer coalesce.
ethan: Ok. Short-term mitigation: add a flag to route <16-token requests to the FA_v2 kernel (lower per-call overhead) while we tune v3. e.g. feature flag `attn.kernel.route_shortseq_to_v2` on by default off.
li: Agreed. Also we should surface these metrics in the canary dashboard: p50/p95/p99, avg_batch_size, kernel_launches/sec, memcpy_bytes/sec, KV_hit_ratio, GPU_SM_util. Those will make the impact obvious.
ops-bot: Canary plan template: create flag, roll to internal-prod (0.01%), then eu-west-1 (1%) for 15 minutes, collect metrics, then 10% global for 10 minutes. Scheduled deploy window: 2026-03-20T18:00:00Z. :calendar:
mira: I'll add a perf CI job that simulates 10k QPS with 70% of requests at 1-8 tokens and instruments avg batch size + kernel path tags. Will push artifacts to S3 and post link here.
ethan: Let's also make the flag auto-trigger rollback: if p99 latency increases >10% or avg_batch_size < 1.6 for 5 continuous minutes, revert routing.
li: One more: check paged-attn and fused-attn fallbacks. The v3 path may be disabling kernel fusion for some shape combos, which increases kernel calls even further. Add a unit microbenchmark for shapes [B=128,S=4], [B=256,S=2].
perf-bot: Test matrix queued: shapes=[(128,4),(256,2),(64,8)], kernels=[fa_v2,fa_v3,fused], concurrency=[64,128,256], duration=3m each. Results will be posted to #eng-runtime/perf when ready.
mira: Great. I'll open the flag PR (flags repo) and draft the runbook steps (rollback, telemetry checks, post-mortem checklist). Will also stub the CI test today.
ethan: For rollout phases in the runbook, recommend: 0.1% internal -> 1% eu-west -> 10% global -> 50% -> full, with human sign-off between phases. Add a hard kill switch in the edge router too.
li: And schedule a post-rollback profiling run to gather more traces to inform batch-window tuning. We should try 1.2ms and 1.6ms windows in perf tests and compare.
mira: :thumbsup: I'll coordinate and ping infra for the router kill-switch path.
ops-bot: Action items created: FLAG-3212 (route_shortseq_to_v2), PERF-847 (shortseq bench), RUNBOOK-56 (fa_v3_rollback). Assigned to mira, ethan, li. Deadline: 2026-03-22.
ethan: Thanks — nice catch. Once the flag is in, we should monitor for any doubling in request count to v2 (cost implications) and include cost delta in the dashboard.
mira: Yep — will include cost delta and MV exposure. Will post initial artifacts in this thread when available.
